I ran the adapter suite at `0bcd0d5` and all 86 tests passed. I also reproduced three streaming cases worth covering before merge.

- **Malformed JSON still reaches the client.** If the provider sends `{` and finishes the tool call, the adapter forwards that fragment and closes the block normally. The client cannot parse the input. If fragments have already gone out, appending `{}` cannot repair them. Validate before emitting the tool input, or end the stream with an error if validation fails after deltas have gone out.
- **Large valid inputs get slower with each fragment.** The adapter runs `trimStart()` on the whole growing buffer for every delta. In a local Node 24 run with 8,000 fragments of 64 characters each, the PR took about 214 ms versus 18 ms on the base. Classify the prefix once per tool block.
- **A reused tool index can lose valid arguments.** When a tool emits `null`, then a text delta closes the block, a valid object on that same upstream index becomes `{}`. Reset the argument state when the block closes.

Thanks for reproducing these. Pushed 46196bb addressing all three, plus the cubic P2.

- **Malformed JSON:** tool arguments that start with `{` still stream as deltas. When the upstream finishes the tool call (finish_reason, or a text delta follows) the accumulated buffer is parsed. If it is not a JSON object, deltas have already gone out and cannot be repaired, so the stream now ends with an Anthropic `error` event instead of a normal `content_block_stop`. A cut-off upstream with no finish_reason closes as before.
- **Slow large inputs:** the prefix is classified once per tool block from the first non-whitespace character, so there is no per-delta `trimStart()` on the growing buffer.
- **Reused tool index:** the block's argument buffer and kind are reset when it closes, so a valid object on the same upstream index after a `null` call is forwarded intact.

Added three tests in `anthropic-messages-adapter.spec.ts` (malformed `{` ends with an error, no `trimStart` calls across 4,000 fragments, null-then-object on one index). They fail on the previous head and the file passes after (89 tests).

This change was prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant and submitted by the account owner.
